apps.name: AirCard-iOS
apps.subtitle: Apple Wallet card skins, passcode themes and wallpapers
apps.localizedDescription: Customize Apple Wallet card artwork, lock screen passcode dialers and PosterBoard wallpapers directly on device, without a jailbreak. Requires iOS 27 or newer, LocalDevVPN running in loopback mode, and Developer Mode pairing.

versions.localizedDescription:
## What's Changed in v1.3.2 🚀

This update brings full feature parity with AirCard macOS v1.2.6, restores robust card discovery across all iOS versions, introduces automatic bank/network recognition with custom card nicknames, delivers an ultra-fast tunnel cache (0.02s connections), and completely resolves wallpaper flashing for Collections and Mercury wallpapers.

### 💳 Wallet Card Discovery & Bank Identification
• **Universal Wallet Log Parser**: Ported the proven `WalletScanParser` from AirCard macOS. Captures cards from `Dashboard loading (...): for SOO+`, `passIDs[InSession]`, `passIDs[global]`, and modern JSON NFC activations (`"identifier": "HEX"`).
• **Automatic Bank & Network Detection**: Recognizes Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, Discover, and JCB via applet AIDs during selection.
• **Card Nicknames (Rename)**: Added a direct **Rename** button (✏️) so you can give your cards friendly names like *"Monobank"*, *"Salary Card"*, or *"Revolut"*, safely persisted in app settings.
• **28-Character Fallback Token Matcher**: Restores dependable card discovery on devices where standard log patterns are redacted.

### ⚡ Ultra-Fast Tunnel Routing (from 10s to 0.02s!)
• **Working Route Caching**: `rust-core` now caches the active RSD connection route (`LAST_WORKING_ROUTE`), eliminating repeated port and interface scanning.
• **RSD-First Priority**: Connects directly via RemoteXPC on port 49152, bypassing slow Lockdown retries and broken pipes on iOS 18+.
• **Eliminated Loopback Policy Drops**: Removed local loopback attempts that caused `policy drop` control channel errors.

### 🖼 Wallpapers (.tendies) — Collections & Mercury Fixes
• **Dual Injection on iOS 18+**: Wallpapers are now injected into both their primary bundle (`com.apple.WallpaperKit.CollectionsPoster` or `com.apple.MercuryPoster`) and the modern iOS 18+ application container (`com.apple.Posters.CollectionsPosterApp` / `com.apple.Posters.MercuryPosterApp`).
• **Metadata Synchronization**: Fixed a critical issue where `Wallpaper.plist`'s numeric identifier was randomized out-of-sync with `suggestionMetadata.plist` (`7400.DYNAMIC`), causing wallpapers like Windows 11 to vanish from the Lock Screen gallery.
• **Mercury Wallpaper Support**: Added recognition for `mercury-descriptors` container folders and registered `com.apple.Posters.MercuryPosterApp` in `PersistedPosterContainerBundleIdentifiers`.
• **NeoSpring Respring**: Instant springboard reload to apply wallpaper preferences immediately.

### 🧪 Quality & Testing
• All 24 unit tests passing (`TendiesEngineTests`, `WalletScanParserTests`, `CardPhotoCropTests`, `CardPhotoPickerTests`).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Mak5er/AirCard-iOS/compare/v1.3.1...v1.3.2

apps.name: AniBaka
apps.subtitle: 跨平台番剧聚合、媒体播放与弹幕客户端
apps.localizedDescription: AniBaka 是一个基于 Flutter 的跨平台番剧聚合与媒体播放客户端，支持多番剧源、弹幕、字幕、离线缓存与本地媒体库，并提供动漫实时超分辨率画质增强。

versions.localizedDescription:
### 新增

- Windows 新增 AnimeJaNai 实时超分：播放器底栏一键开关，可与 Anime4K、DLSS 叠加；支持 TensorRT / DirectML 后端自动选择，提供质量、均衡、性能三档与原版、Sharp1 两种模型，附细节锐化、亮度、对比度、饱和度、伽马调节及原画/超分同帧对比。
- AnimeJaNai 可选 RIFE 补帧：支持 2×、3×、4× 倍率，提供完整（原分辨率处理）与快速（最高 540p 处理）两种方案。
- 新增“画质设置”面板，整合 AnimeJaNai 与 DLSS 全部选项；播放器内长按增强按钮或进入“实验室”页面均可打开，运行状态、安装进度与诊断信息集中展示。
- Windows 播放器底栏常显 Anime4K / AnimeJaNai / DLSS 开关，点按切换、长按进入画质设置，无需先在实验室开启。
- 评论区改版：正文按 Markdown / BBCode 渲染，评论中的时间点自动识别为跳转链接，点击可seek到对应进度或指定集数；表情贴图正常显示，加载时改用骨架占位。

### 优化

- 更新优化内置源规则
- DLSS 与 AnimeJaNai 运行库改由组织维护的 media-kit fork 统一打包，应用内不再捆绑原生桥接代码，减小安装体积。
- 充分优化日志系统
- 优化了一些小细节

### 使用说明

- AnimeJaNai 仅支持 Windows；首次启用需联网下载运行库与模型（补帧组件约 441 MiB），下载过程可取消，TensorRT 后端首次使用需编译引擎。
- 后端设为“自动”时，支持的 NVIDIA 显卡优先使用 TensorRT，其余显卡使用 DirectML。
- AnimeJaNai 模型按 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 分发，仅限非商业用途。

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/AniBakaBaka/AniBaka/compare/5.2.3+1020...5.2.4+1101

apps.name: Apollo for Reddit - GLASS
apps.subtitle: Apollo-Reborn build with Liquid Glass patch
apps.localizedDescription:
Apollo-Reborn is the community-maintained Apollo sideload build powered by the Apollo-Reborn tweak.

It restores custom API support, media fixes, uploads, inline media, translation, saved categories, Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, Liquid Glass support on iOS 26+, and the rest of the project’s ongoing fixes and enhancements.

These sources are intended for AltStore Classic, SideStore, and Feather. Apollo-Reborn is not compatible with AltStore PAL.

Choose the source variant that matches how you sideload:

• Standard: full app bundle with Apollo’s working extensions plus Apollo-Reborn widgets
• No Extensions: strips app extensions, including widgets, to reduce App ID usage on free Apple IDs
• GLASS: adds the Liquid Glass iOS 26 patch and bundled Liquid Glass icon catalog
• No Extensions + GLASS: combines both options

The extension-bearing builds (Standard and GLASS) register about 7 App IDs, one per bundled app extension. A free Apple ID can register 10 App IDs per 7 days, so a clean single install fits, but it is easy to exceed if you install under more than one bundle ID, reinstall within the same week, or sideload other extension-bearing apps. If an install fails with an App ID error, use a No Extensions build (1 App ID) or wait for older App IDs to expire. A paid Apple Developer account has a much higher cap.

This project is not affiliated with Apollo or Christian Selig.

apps.name: ARMSX2
apps.subtitle: PlayStation 2 emulator for ARM64
apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- microVU0: compute the VU1 register window's address at run time
- Tests: a persisted VU0 program that uses the window onto VU1's registers
- Android: link the core with emulated TLS when the minimum API is below 29
- iOS: give the layout editor and the manifest skin their own views
- iOS: split the patch and skin library stores by their own sections
- iOS: split navigation and gameplay views into one file per view
- iOS: split the controls and skin files along their types
- iOS: split the dynamic backgrounds into one file per background

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261112...37ed35b88fe9a0164369c8042f2c9aa707e33667

versions.localizedDescription:
## Changes

- Recover downloads when Apple returns an empty HTTP 500 by retrying the version-pinned request through the bag’s update endpoint.
- Update ApplePackage to 2.0.3 with Swift 6.2 compatibility fixes.
- Report Keychain save failures before completing login, and preserve stored data when loading fails.
- Improve empty account layout, editable device identifiers, and account table column widths.
- Remove personal metadata from bundled installation certificates and omit the CA private key.
- Explicitly clear development teams for release builds and check packaged artifacts before publication.

## Installation certificate

The local installation CA was replaced to remove personal metadata. If you use OTA installation, install and trust the new certificate from Settings after updating.

The release contains an unsigned iOS IPA and a macOS ZIP without a personal development team.

apps.name: BCD
apps.subtitle: Windows games on iPhone and iPad
apps.localizedDescription: A fast, controller-friendly launcher that runs Windows games on iOS and iPadOS with Steam and GOG built in, powered by Wine, FEX and Metal via DXMT.

versions.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

This build brings **The Last of Us Part I**, **frame generation** (with your own copy of Lossless Scaling, with Apple's MetalFX, and an Apple VideoToolbox experiment), **live upscaling**, BCD's built-in JIT helper inside LiveContainer, and a set of new controls, store and settings features. Everything new is off until you turn it on, except the fixes.

## The Last of Us Part I

The Last of Us Part I now runs on BCD. It was tested on an iPhone with 12 GB of memory (A19 Pro); devices with less memory are not tested.

- **Before you start:** on the game's page, **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**. The recommended settings carry everything below, and the game starts at 30 FPS.
- **Set the game's own graphics to the lowest and AMD FSR to Performance.** This is required: in the game's own graphics settings, choose the lowest preset for everything, and set AMD FSR to **Performance**. BCD reminds you once, before the first start, as it does for the other demanding games.
- **First start:** the game builds its shaders in the main menu, about 20 minutes the first time. Let it finish in the menu, then quit and start the game again. Later starts read them back from BCD's shader cache in about a minute and a half.
- **Fixed for this game, and for any Direct3D 12 game that does the same:**
  - **No lighting, dark and wrong colours, characters not drawn.** The game clears its lighting work through a typed buffer view with four different values, and BCD wrote the first value into every word. Each value now goes into its own channel of every element, as Direct3D 12 does.
  - **Closed by iOS as the first level loaded.** The game creates about 126,000 pipelines at every start and draws under 1 % of them, and BCD kept a compiled shader library for each, 2.8 GB in all. With the recommended settings, a pipeline's libraries wait in BCD's shader cache until it is first drawn: peak memory went from 8.1 GB to 5.7 GB.
  - **Hundreds of thousands of needless exceptions.** Every indirect draw cost an exception on iOS (6,000 to 15,000 a second in play), because BCD read the clock the Windows way. BCD now reads the CPU's own counter.
- **Frame generation:** the recommended settings turn on Lossless Scaling frame generation (2×) for this game. It works when you own Lossless Scaling on Steam and have set it up once (see below). Without it, the game runs as before.
- **How it plays:** on an iPhone with an A19 Pro, with the game held at 30 FPS and Lossless Scaling frame generation on, it plays at 60 FPS for the first few minutes, then at about 40 FPS once the phone warms up.

## New

- **Frame generation with your own copy of Lossless Scaling (experimental):** adds one to three frames between the game's own, for Direct3D 11 and Direct3D 12 games. No motion vectors and no help from the game are needed.
  - **Setup, once:** sign in to Steam in BCD, then **Settings › Graphics › Lossless Scaling › Check my purchase and download from Steam**.
  - **Use:** on a game's page, **Display › Lossless Scaling frame generation**: 2×, 3× or 4×. The in-game menu shows its state and changes it while you play.
  - **Lossless Scaling is not part of BCD.** BCD asks Steam whether your account owns it, downloads it with your account, and keeps the file sealed on this device. A game reads only the frame generation shaders from it, and they are removed when the game ends. The purchase is checked again every week; **Remove it from this device** deletes everything.
- **Live MetalFX frame generation and upscaling (experimental):** a game's page has **Display › Live upscaling and frame generation**.
  - **Frame generation:** runs at the game's own resolution, before the picture is enlarged, so it costs less. You can turn it on and off from the in-game menu while you play. It pauses by itself while the GPU is too busy for it. iOS 26 or later.
  - **Upscaling:** **MetalFX upscaling** now also has **To the screen**, which enlarges the game's picture to fit the screen, for Direct3D 11 and Direct3D 12. With live upscaling on, the factor can be changed from the in-game menu while you play.
- **Apple frame interpolation (experiment, iOS 26):**
  - **Settings › Graphics › Experimental › Test Apple frame interpolation on this device** measures what VideoToolbox's low-latency frame interpolation can do on your device, with no game needed. On an A19 Pro it took pictures up to 1920x1080, in about 4 ms a pair at 1280x720.
  - **Apple frame interpolation** on a game's page uses it in a game.
- **LiveContainer:** BCD's built-in JIT helper now works inside LiveContainer, through LiveContainer's Helper Process Support (LiveContainer 3.8.13 or later; turn on **Helper Process Support** for BCD in LiveContainer). Outside LiveContainer, or with that switch off, nothing changes.
- **JIT off, tap to fix:** the **JIT off** label on Home now turns on JIT when you tap it, as **Settings › JIT › Enable JIT** does. On an upright phone, the update label beside it says **Update**.
- **Touch controls:**
  - **Floating sticks:** in the in-game menu, **Touch & rumble › Floating sticks**. A controller stick's ring appears where your thumb lands near it. Off by default; it can be saved per game.
  - **Six more built-in layouts:** Left-handed controller, Sticks in the middle, Handheld controller, Retro pad, Racing pad and Small controller, in the layout list after Full controller and PC keyboard.
- **Controller as keys (experimental):** on a game's page, **Controls › Controller as keys when the game has no controller support**. If the game never reads a controller in its first 25 seconds, your controller drives the mouse and keys instead.
- **External drives:** a drive's sheet in **Settings › Storage › External drives** has **Test speed**. For a slow drive, `drive-gentle-writes = 1` writes Steam downloads with fewer writers at once.
- **Steam Cloud:** a game's cloud section lists every save a sync would move up or down before anything moves, and **Check again** compares again.
- **Auto-tune, ask first:** **Settings › Logs › Ask before trying a fix** (off by default). Auto-tune then shows the fix it wants to try and waits for **Try it**, **Not now** or **Stop**. A kept fix can be undone.
- **Amazon Games (experimental):** **Settings › Accounts › Amazon Games** signs in to Amazon and lists, installs and starts your Amazon Games library. Off by default; not yet tried with a real account.
- **What does this mean?** BCD's most common library and Steam messages have a button that explains them in plain words.
- **Logs:**
  - **Settings › Logs › Make big logs smaller before sending** (off by default) leaves out most repeated diagnostic lines from a large log before it is sent; the file on the device stays whole.
  - `benchmark-line = 1` writes a one-line summary at the end of a session: frame rate and lows, least free memory, swap and JIT peaks, and the switches in force.
- **Experiments for slower games,** off by default:
  - **Settings › Memory & performance › Speed and power › Tell iOS a game is running** asks iOS to treat the game as interactive work and logs the fast cores' clock.
  - `env.MADEIRA_FEX_CALLRET_LEAN = 1` makes the emulator's return from a call two instructions shorter.

## Fixes and improvements

> **Tried a game on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** A game keeps the settings it had until you reset them. On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**, then check that **Options › Auto-tune › Auto-tune this game** is on, and start the game again.

- **Direct3D 12:** the two engine fixes under The Last of Us Part I above apply to every Direct3D 12 game:
  - a typed buffer UAV clear writes each value into its own channel;
  - no exception for each indirect command.
- **Direct3D 12, experiment:** `typed-view-unlocked = 1` makes typed buffer views outside the device's view lock, for games that create tens of thousands of them a second from several threads.
- **MetalFX frame generation:** a game whose picture size keeps changing no longer rebuilds the interpolator each time. This was the cause of a graphics-driver error with frame generation on in some games.
- **Starting a game:** Auto-tune read the previous session's log at every start, and with a large log that kept a CPU core busy for up to two minutes while the next game loaded. The same reading now takes a small fraction of that time, with identical results.
- **Demanding games:** the one-time reminder before the first start now says to set AMD FSR to **Performance** (it said Balanced or Performance).
- **Auto-tune** knows three more cases:
  - a game closed by iOS while BCD held a shader library for tens of thousands of pipelines;
  - the typed buffer clear;
  - the clock exceptions.

## Recommended settings

- **The Last of Us Part I** (v25): the settings it was tested with, Lossless Scaling frame generation included, a 30 FPS start and the reminder to set the game's own graphics to the lowest and AMD FSR to Performance.

An x86-64 PC emulator for iOS. Fathom runs x86-64 Linux programs on an iPhone or iPad by translating them to ARM64 as they execute, using FEXCore - the dynamic recompiler behind FEX-Emu - with a native SwiftUI front end.

- Fewer `OutOfMemoryError: pthread_create` crashes on installs without extended address space

# Steam64 setup, one step at a time

**Experimental prerelease · Build145 · Known issue: Steam can freeze after the third game exit. This update improves setup; it does not fix that stability issue.**

## What’s new

- **Install Steam64 in the launcher:** downloads the matched Steam/browser packages from Valve over HTTPS, verifies sizes/SHA-256 and installs with rollback. Cancel/retry, Verify/Repair and Return to previous environment are available.
- **Four clear actions:** Install Steam → Connect LocalDevVPN → Pair this device → Enable JIT. Runtime preparation is automatic, signing/address checks remain mandatory, completed steps are checked/skipped and the view follows the next action.
- **Pair in iDeck:** starts the existing on-device pairing immediately with live instructions/PIN, without hunting through JIT settings. iOS calls the pairing host Madeira. Advanced methods/import/recovery/account/auto-start settings are collapsed.
- **Data stays yours:** the original environment remains intact; no auth cache, game or save is silently transferred. Use Valve’s own login and Steam Guard yourself.

## Install and test

Download `iDeck-0.1.3-alpha.6-build145.ipa` and `SHA256SUMS`, verify the hash, then sign/sideload using your own coherent development main/helper profiles. Keep `MadeiraJITHelper.appex` and debugging permission; signing alone does not activate JIT. Back up saves and keep the same app identity when upgrading—uninstalling can erase local data.

Open iDeck and follow the highlighted setup step; fully close/reopen when prompted after installing Steam64. For on-device pairing use iOS27; iOS26 offers pairing-file import. Activate JIT again for each new app process.

The IPA includes the local runtime and pinned source-built open support components, **no Valve Steam client/libcef, games, accounts, maintainer profile or pairing file**. The installer acquires the client from Valve. Both source companions, relink, license/audit and inventory/checksum assets accompany this release.

## What was verified

The user reports Build144 installation can complete. Build145 passed host ordering/skip/restart/signing/VA checks, installer/rollback/privacy regressions, existing JIT integration checks and full Xcode compilation. Its separate Fresh Test version was development-signed, installed/read back and opened on an iPhone15ProMax; original iDeck was preserved. The public ad-hoc IPA was audited (1480files, no findings), and its105-input relink ran with all30TEXT section hashes matching.

The complete revised145 first-run UI, another-device sideload/JIT, new Steam login and repeated gameplay have **not** received a new acceptance result; the public IPA was not installed again after ad-hoc packaging. iPad, Bluetooth and arbitrary games are not validated by this release. Full independent-machine/offline runtime rebuilding is not claimed.

## Limits that still matter

- **Third game return may freeze Steam.** Report the first failing stage and game-cycle count.
- Steam64 does **not** enlarge the device’s virtual address space. Unsupported layouts can still fail;32-bit games/helpers may still hit separate limits. Guards remain enabled.
- The compatibility snapshot is **Steam manifest1769025840 (January22,2026), CEF126**, held to its matched components. It is not the latest Steam/Chromium and has security/compatibility limitations; future snapshots need fresh review.
- Game support remains limited. No DRM, authentication or anti-cheat bypass is provided. Never post credentials, Steam Guard data, pairing files, profiles or raw personal logs.

See [the four-step guide](https://github.com/kuscholar/iDeck/blob/v0.1.3-alpha.6/docs/STEAM64_SETUP.md), [Build145 evidence](https://github.com/kuscholar/iDeck/blob/v0.1.3-alpha.6/docs/release/BUILD145_RESULTS.md) and the bilingual README.

# Iridium 0.2.0

Download your Steam games directly in Iridium, manage repairs and updates, and try the updated Windows runtime. Game support remains experimental.

## Download

**[Download Iridium (.ipa)](https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/releases/download/v0.2.0/Iridium-unsigned.ipa)**

Requires **iOS or iPadOS 18+**, JIT, and games you own. You only need the IPA to install; supply your own game files or download owned games from Steam.

## Install

1. Sign and install the IPA and helper with a compatible sideloading tool, or import it into LiveContainer using its supported JIT setup.
2. Open Iridium and configure JIT in **Launch Support**.
3. Open **Downloads → Steam** to sign in and queue a game, or use **Add Game** to import a game folder. Choose its executable, add it to your library, then press **Play**.

For standalone installation, preserve `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true` in both Iridium's final app signature and provisioning profile. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation.

Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. Steam repairs and updates keep older installations; saves stored inside an older game folder may need to be copied manually to the new one. Keep that older folder until you have checked your saves.

## What's new

- **Steam downloads in the app.** Sign in with a password or QR code, with Steam Guard support, browse your library, and choose download language, unprotected branch, 32/64-bit files, and owned DLC.
- **A download queue with verification and repair.** Pause, resume, retry, and prioritize downloads. Check for updates or repair downloaded files while keeping the previous installation.
- **Clearer storage warnings.** Download checks use the space available to Iridium and account for verified partial files. **Download Anyway** can bypass an estimated-space warning for one attempt; file verification and real out-of-space errors remain enforced.
- **Updated Windows runtime.** Includes 32-bit WoW64 support and D3D9/D3D12 updates. Support still varies by game and device.
- **Game prerequisite installers.** Run supported setup steps included with a game, or choose **Game Options → Run Installer** for an EXE or MSI installer you provide. Some installers need interaction. Closing the player requests cancellation; Iridium keeps observing the runtime's exit and reports when a restart is required.
- **Reduced duplicate runtime data.** Identical Windows runtime files share one packaged copy. The main app's anonymous ad-hoc signature carries only the increased-memory-limit request; helpers remain unsigned until you sign them.

## Known issues

- Physical-device compatibility for these changes has not been established. Some games may fail to launch or have graphics, video, audio, input, save, or shutdown problems. Skyrim speech and mouse attack issues remain unverified.
- Keep Iridium open while downloading. Downloads pause when the app goes into the background and need to be resumed. Real-account downloads and recovery after Wi-Fi or network loss still need device testing.
- Steam Cloud, Workshop, Steam Families library discovery, password-protected branches, and desktop Steam services are not included. Games that require Steamworks/DRM, anti-cheat, or other unsupported runtime features may not launch after downloading.
- Updates keep older game copies and need extra storage. **Download Anyway** does not create free space; exhausting device storage can also prevent other apps from saving.
- JIT and available memory depend on your device and signing setup; LiveContainer and standalone results can differ. Built-in JIT requires standalone Iridium, debugging permission, a valid pairing file, and LocalDevVPN. Hosted Iridium uses external JIT. Recipient signing, LiveContainer hosting, and game prerequisite success still need device testing.

The other release files are for source access, rebuilding, and download verification:

- Download both `Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01` and `.part02` for the complete matching source package.
- `Iridium-source-guide.zip` contains license notices, source records, and build/relink instructions.
- `SHA256SUMS` verifies the IPA, both source parts, and the source guide.

Download all five release files into one folder, then run:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
cat Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01 Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part02 > Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz
unzip Iridium-source-guide.zip
shasum -a 256 -c Iridium-source-guide/ASSEMBLED-SHA256SUMS

Independent IPA inspection confirmed the exact anonymous XML/DER entitlement carrier with no CMS payload or team identity, eight unsigned non-main native binaries, strict bundle verification, runtime hashes, and ZIP modes and symlinks. Unchanged runtime component outputs were reused after provenance checks. These checks do not establish real-account login, owned-game downloads, game compatibility, recipient signing, or physical-device behavior.

4. **追番与观看历史**：设置备份不含这两类数据。需要保留时，先在旧版完成 Bangumi／WebDAV 同步，再在新版导入设置后同步相应数据。

**设置备份也不包含下载记录。** 确认所需数据已转移后再卸载旧版。

### 新增

- 从推荐页「热门番组」「本季新番」等更多列表进入详情再返回时，不再重置到列表顶部（[#29](https://github.com/LinkPass888/Kazumi-Swift/issues/29)）
- AniSkip 跳片头、片尾使用精确跳转，不再停在目标之前的关键帧
- 修复退出播放器或换集后，迟到的画中画取帧任务访问已销毁内核导致的崩溃

### 优化

- 详情页在宽屏（可用宽度 ≥ 860）改三栏：封面、条目信息、简介三等分；「开始观看」固定在右下角，竖栏不再重复一遍番名

- 「我的」页最近观看卡片：番名支持两行，补上播放／重看角标与来源、时间
- 最近搜索胶囊按文字宽度排布，空间不足时整颗换行，不再挤在等宽格子里
- 设置页的横向边距交回系统，Duo 合上时不再压到右边栏
- 观看历史右上角「清空」与返回按钮同色，不再跟主题色走
- 应用内的仓库链接换到新仓库名 Kazumi-Swift，不再多走一次旧名跳转

apps.localizedDescription: Run ARM64 Linux applications and desktop environments on iOS without a jailbreak, virtual machine, or JIT.

versions.localizedDescription:
# LinuxRunner v1.0.1

Linux on your iPhone and iPad. This update adds iPad desktop adaptations, brings Arch Linux ARM into the setup workflow and improves package recovery and desktop sessions.

## What's New

- **iPad support:** window-aware desktop sizing, hardware-keyboard desktop shortcuts and the shared touch/pointer interface. Tested on a physical iPad.
- **Arch Linux ARM:** install signed packages, use `pacman` and explore an experimental Openbox desktop with LXQt Panel and PCManFM-Qt.
- **One setup workflow:** **Distributions → Set Up Linux…** installs a distribution or configures an existing environment while preserving its files and accounts.

The maintainer reports a working Arch graphical desktop and graphical application launches on a physical iPhone using **build 897**. Telegram Desktop has been tested on Arch Linux ARM with login, sending messages and calls. The supplied iPhone capture shows its welcome screen.

## Improvements

Arch desktop defaults provide a visible panel, wallpaper and file manager without replacing the user's normal LXQt configuration. Managed graphical launches share the active account's authenticated X11 context. Desktop startup status and Qt diagnostics are more useful when a component fails.

IPA packaging now includes an ad-hoc code signature and a standard ZIP layout. It still needs a compatible signing/provisioning method for ordinary device installation.

## Bug Fixes

- Arch terminal termios2 compatibility.
- Signed cached-package recovery and consistent handling of orphaned GCC ownership/obsolete recovery state.
- Qt X11 launch-context failures and desktop profile defaults.
- Reopening existing desktop sessions and readiness after component crashes.
- ARM64 vDSO executable mapping and covered filesystem/syscall compatibility gaps.

## Supported Distributions

| Distribution | Experience |
| --- | --- |
| Debian GNU/Linux 13 ARM64 | Recommended terminal and LinuxRunner Desktop; KDE Plasma remains experimental. |
| Arch Linux ARM | Terminal, `pacman` and experimental Openbox/LXQt-component desktop. |
| Alpine Linux 3.24 ARM64 | Small terminal environment with `apk`; graphical compatibility remains experimental. |

## Installation

Download the release IPA and sign/install it with your preferred compatible sideloading tool, such as Sideloadly or AltStore Classic. Then use **Distributions → Set Up Linux…** to install Linux inside the app.

See the [installation guide](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner#installation) and [Linux setup walkthrough](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/blob/v1.0.1/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md). When updating, back up important files and preserve the existing app identity and App Group configuration. Do not uninstall the app as a repair step.

## Known Limitations

The application interprets ARM64 Linux userspace; it does not boot a Linux kernel, require JIT or use hardware virtualization. System-call and application coverage is incomplete. The configured minimum is iOS/iPadOS 15.0; model/OS compatibility is not universal. iPad support has been physically tested. An older iPhone 11/iOS 17 launch-black-screen report is unresolved.

Arch desktop, Debian KDE Plasma and Metal acceleration remain experimental. Arch Plasma/Wayland is unavailable. Some Arch GTK/glycin programs still encounter write-seal compatibility problems. Large applications can be slow or exceed memory limits. iOS/iPadOS may suspend or terminate the app; saved files persist, running processes do not survive termination.

## Downloads

- **LinuxRunner-1.0.1.ipa** — ad-hoc signed, without an Apple provisioning profile. Install with your preferred compatible signing/sideloading method.
- **LinuxRunner-1.0.1-source.tar.gz** — matching application source and build scripts, pinned build dependencies, matching Alpine source inputs and terminal-renderer sources.
- **LICENSES.txt** — project and third-party license notices.
- **SHA256SUMS** — checksums for the IPA, source archive and license notices.

The IPA is **14,646,386 bytes**. Verify the original download before signing it; signing changes its checksum.

```text
c571c7ae1dd8ab641930e513254866658dc94f0bee370f1d2623cd462f0fa2ca  LinuxRunner-1.0.1.ipa
```

GitHub automatic source archives omit submodule contents. Use the separately attached source asset for the dependency-inclusive source distribution.

## Feedback and License

[Report reproducible problems through GitHub Issues](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/issues/new/choose), including your device, OS, app version/build, distribution and diagnostic report. Review logs/screenshots for personal information before attaching them.

LinuxRunner derives from [iSH](https://github.com/ish-app/ish) through [ios-linuxkit](https://github.com/rcarmo/ios-linuxkit). The combined application is GPL-3.0-covered; upstream copyright, contribution-specific terms, App Store terms and third-party notices are preserved. See the repository's [license](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/blob/v1.0.1/LICENSE.md) and [third-party notices](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/blob/v1.0.1/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

# ⚠️This build is OUTDATED. Please use [nightly version](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/releases/tag/nightly) instead.

# LiveContainer 3.8.0

> [!Warning]
> The standalone version requires **SideStore 0.6.2+** or **AltStore 2.2.1+** for installation.
> To install LiveContainer with built-in SideStore (`LiveContainer+SideStore.ipa`), please use [Impactor](https://github.com/khcrysalis/Impactor) or [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader). See [our installation guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/installation/lc_sidestore) for details.

# New Features

## Storage Management

- Added a new storage management view with a breakdown of app bundles, containers, temporary files, app group data, tweaks, and other files. (Hidden apps' size is included in "other" section until unlocked)
- Added per-app storage details, including app bundle size, container sizes, and last-used date.
- Added actions to clean temporary files and caches, including guest app caches and LiveContainer's own caches.

## Multiple LiveContainers
- Added configurable launch priority for multiple LiveContainer instances, making shared-app shortcuts choose available instances in the order you prefer. (#1367)

## Share to Apps in LiveContainer
Added a share extension to LiveContainer. When you share a URL or a file from iOS's share sheet, LiveContainer will ask which app you would like to open the URL/file in, so the old share to LiveContainer shortcut method is no longer needed. When an ipa file is shared in this way, LiveContainer will ask if you want to install it in LiveContainer or in the built-in SideStore (if installed) (#1357)

## Multitasking

- Added per-app multitask preferences. Each app can now follow the global setting, always launch in multitask mode, or avoid multitask mode. (#1208)
- Improved multitask dock behavior: the dock can be made smaller, hidden more cleanly, and has improved padding. (#1228, #1250)
- Added more multitask window animations and improved native-window scene handling.
- URL schemes and `open-url` payloads can be passed to already-running multitask apps and native windows.

## JIT
- Added StosDebug support as a JIT enabler.

## TweakLoader
You can now disable tweaks in the "Tweaks" page in LiveContainer's UI. by @SAOMDVN

# Improvements
- Added support for manually setting a container's IDFV. (#1194)
- IDFV spoofing works even when Tweakloader is not loaded.
- Reworked signing logic for tweaks and app installation, with multithreaded signing support.
- Download alerts now block tab switching while a download is in progress.
- Crash reports are shown in a sheet instead of a large alert for better performance on newer iOS versions.
- Add a "Clear Notification" button (#1388)
- Added some popular NSBonjourServices keys so apps can discover AirPlay devices and remote pairing pairable hosts in the local network. (#1417)

# Bug Fixes

- Fixed `livecontainer://open-url` dropping the deep link when launching an app from a cold start. (#1339)
- Fixed the Add to Home Screen menu failing or behaving incorrectly by replacing the SwiftUI context menu implementation. (#1209)
- Fixed a crash when opening Container Preferences if the app did not contain an `en.lproj` path. (#1239)
- Fixed apps and AltStore sources not being searchable in some cases. (#1365, #1368)
- Fixed converting a shared app back to private after aborting an install with the same bundle identifier, which could leave stale container state behind. (#1347)
- Fixed shortcuts and JIT flows getting stuck on a busy LiveContainer instance instead of using another available instance. (#1386)
- Fixed file picker not workings for some apps because Tweakloader is not loaded after enabling "Hide LiveContainer from dyld API". (#1430)
- Fixed several app launch compatibility issues on iOS 26.5 beta, and some multitask/JIT app launches. (#1300, #1310, #1329)
- Fixed multitask keyboard focus issues on iOS 17.4+, including cases where the keyboard would not appear, Passwords would immediately close, or video playback would freeze in multitask mode. (#1402, #844, #870)
- Added support for iOS 27 developer beta. (#1394, #1417, #1416)
- Fix background downloads in multitask apps (choosing "Keep App Extensions (Register App ID for Each Extension)" is required). (#1415)

# Localization

- Updated translations. Added Spanish translation by @Deci8BelioS

# Credits

Thanks to everyone who contributed code, fixes, testing, and reports for this release, including @boa-z, @ruri1208, @Project516, @yazdipour, @stossy11, and @SAOMDVN.

Great thanks to everyone who helped translate LiveContainer.

Games come with a library, Steam sign-in and installs, controller and touch controls, and keyboard, mouse and trackpad input. Requires an iPhone on iOS 26 or later with JIT enabled through StikDebug.

versions.localizedDescription:
### New
- **More stores.** Madeira has a new **GOG** section: sign in with GOG's own login page, see your library, download and update games with the DLC you own, verify and repair them, and play with Galaxy achievements and stats (Madeira stands in for GOG Galaxy). A new **EA app** section: sign in, see your library and download games without the EA app. A new **itch.io** store shows your itch.io games and free games, and downloads and installs them, .7z archives included. **Epic Games** now handles game downloads and cloud saves together.
- **Store tabs.** With more than one store on the library page, a row of tabs at the top (All, Steam, Other, GOG, itch.io, Epic, EA) shows one store at a time. All is the page as before; the tab you pick is remembered.
- **Steam:**
  - DLC downloads with the game, with a switch per DLC
  - beta branches, with beta codes
  - a Workshop page per game
  - achievements
  - choosing the game's language
  - downloading from a PC on the same network
  - faster repairs
  - a switch that turns Steam Cloud off
- **A redesigned library.** Game details pages, a starting screen, and Settings split into pages. You can also turn on a zoomable grid in Settings › Appearance › New library grid.
- **Recommended settings** for many games, with Reset to Recommended. Share Setup sends a game's setup to someone else.
- **Get Help from Claude** on a game's page shares a fixes guide together with your log and config.
- **Translations:** German, Spanish, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Russian.
- **External drives**, save backups and Home Screen shortcuts.
- **Games and downloads keep running** when you leave Madeira.
- **Wine Mono and Wine Gecko** download for you, without Wine's download windows.
- **Graphics:**
  - MetalFX upscaling per game
  - experimental frame generation
  - a per-game picker for the graphics card the game sees
  - FPS limits, including 40 FPS on 120 Hz screens
  - an optional thermal frame cap
- **The performance overlay** has a Column layout that you can drag anywhere on the screen.
- **Controllers and touch controls:**
  - rumble, adaptive triggers and the lightbar on real controllers
  - an optional DualSense / DirectInput mode
  - gyro aim and turbo
  - touch control gesture zones
  - a size slider per touch control, and the editor's panels close when you tap outside them
  - a **Button style** for touch controls: Glass (Liquid Glass) or Solid (plain opaque buttons), in the in-game menu and in Settings › Appearance
- **On iPad:** Command-V pastes into games, and the mouse wheel scrolls.
- **On iPhone:** a Bluetooth or USB mouse works with AssistiveTouch on; mouse-look no longer stops at the screen edges.
- **JIT:** Madeira offers StikDebug when the built-in helper is not available.

### Fixed
- **Native D3D12:** many fixes, including DXIL tessellation, shader caching and faster pipeline builds.
- **Memory and JIT:** many fixes, so large 64-bit and 32-bit games crash less often.
- **Per-game AVX / AVX2**, for games that quit with c000001d.
- **Steam CEG games** can start through Madeira Dock.
- **Launchers that offered to install a game that was already installed:** Madeira Dock now writes the Registry values from a game's install scripts before the start, as Steam's desktop client does.
- **Rockstar Games Launcher / Social Club 2.4.0.296** (the update of 3 November) loads its pages again.
- **The touch controls' Opacity slider** now fades the buttons on iOS 26; it only faded their labels before.
- **Game pills:** the 32-bit / 64-bit and DirectX pills under each game are gone, because they were often wrong. The size pill stays.

### Known issues
- Some Steam games with CEG copy protection still stop with "Madeira Dock stopped" on first start.
- The GOG and EA app sections are new. Please send a log if something goes wrong.

### Install
- Requires **iOS 26 or later**. In-app pairing and the Madeira JIT shortcut need iOS 27.
- If your sideloader asks whether to keep app extensions, keep them: Madeira's in-app JIT runs in one.
- The IPA is ad-hoc signed (no certificate) and carries the app's entitlements, including the increased memory limit. Sideload it with your own Apple ID (SideStore, AltStore, Sideloadly, Plume or similar), which signs it for your device.

### Not included
The Microsoft Visual C++ runtime DLLs are not redistributed (see `legal/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`). Building from source: `tools/fetch-vcruntime.md`.

Thanks to everyone who sent pull requests, logs and test results since 0.1.3.

apps.name: Mangayomi

apps.localizedDescription: Mangayomi is an open-source Flutter app for reading manga, novels, and watching anime across multiple platforms.

versions.localizedDescription:
## Why 0.9.95 and not 1.0.0?

This release has almost everything planned for 1.0.0: a new design, a rebuilt player and hundreds of fixes. But so much has changed that it needs testing on more devices and libraries than we can cover ourselves.

So 0.9.95 is the last step before 1.0.0. The goal now is stability, not new features. If something breaks or looks wrong, please [open an issue](https://github.com/kodjodevf/mangayomi/issues) with your device and app version. 1.0.0 will come once this version has proven solid.

## Highlights

* **Shiori, a new design for the whole app:** every screen has been redrawn on one design system, with new navigation, transitions and an ergonomic pass throughout (#1077).
* **A rebuilt video player:** new controls on phone, desktop and TV, plus video filters, audio delay, and volume, brightness and fit kept between episodes.
* **A tracker with no account:** follow your status, progress, score and dates on the device alone (#1121).
* **Work that keeps going on Android:** downloads, library updates, restores and syncs continue in the background, under one notification (#1092).
* **More control over downloads and updates:** download ahead while reading, download new chapters automatically, and choose which series a library update skips (#1091).

**Before updating:** this is a large release that also touches how your library is stored, so make a backup first (More > Backup and restore).

## Reader

* Zoom with Ctrl (⌘ on macOS) and the mouse wheel; the wheel alone moves a zoomed page.
* With "Navigate to pan" on, tall pages are read row by row before the page turns.
* Split tall images into slices in webtoon mode.
* Choose which chapters next and previous skip: read, filtered or duplicate.
* Rebind the reader's keyboard shortcuts.
* Separate icons for crop borders on and off.
* Pages and zooms follow your finger more closely, and the webtoon strip glides after a fling.
* Decoded images now have a memory limit, so long chapters no longer keep growing in memory.
* Fixed: lost decoded pages for the next chapter when closing the reader, and chapter list rows with a scanlator failing to lay out.

## Video player

* New controls on phone, desktop and TV, with episodes reachable from the top bar and lock and skip under the timeline on mobile.
* **Video filters:** brightness, contrast, saturation, gamma and hue, kept for the next episodes. Gamma is hidden where the video output cannot apply it.
* **Audio delay:** from -5 to +5 seconds.
* Remember volume and brightness between episodes, and keep the fit from one episode to the next.
* New "Turn subtitles on" switch, so episodes can start without subtitles.
* "Use my subtitle style" now really gives the default style back when turned off.
* VAAPI and VDPAU hardware decoding on Linux.
* Rebind the player's keyboard shortcuts.
* Fixed: a freeze in the player's event handling, crashes when chapter marks change, previous and next buttons on mobile, and controls under the camera cutout in landscape.

## Library and browsing

* Swipe sideways to switch between Manga, Anime and Novels, in the library and in Browse.
* Select everything between two entries, in the library and in chapter lists.
* Skip completed series, series with unread chapters or series not started in library updates. The categories' "Skip updates" option now takes effect too.
* The Updates badge counts what was found since you last opened Updates, and clears when you visit.
* Hidden media types are respected everywhere: Browse, Updates, History and the tracker library.
* Browse remembers the Sources or Extensions page picked for each media.
* Recommendation cards use the available space and no longer show HTML tags.
* Fixed: opening Updates and History with orphan chapters, and an empty random entry.

## Downloads

* Download the next 2, 3, 5 or 10 unread chapters while reading.
* Download new chapters after a library update.
* "Delete download after reading" can remove a chapter 1 to 4 back instead, and keeps bookmarked chapters.
* Failed downloads wait before retrying, and follow what a server asks after a 429 or 503.
* Fixed: complete downloads being held back by the series cover, and resumed archives not finishing.

## Tracking

* New on-device tracker, with its own shelf in the tracker library.
* Redrawn tracking card.
* Progress now reaches trackers even if you leave the screen first.

## Extensions

* Updates are found in every repository, and the app says which one they come from. An update from another repository asks for confirmation before it is installed.
* Extension WebViews are hosted for the extension server, including network and media capture.
* Faster extension installs.
* Repositories with empty source lists are supported.
* Fixed: sources that read a setting in their headers failing to install, and video qualities lost with multiple hosters.

## Backup, restore and sync

* Reading time and last-read dates are kept when restoring backups from other apps.
* Anime is kept from backups of unrecognised forks.
* Local archive favorites are included in backups.
* A backup password is only requested when the password is really the problem.
* Refreshing a catalog keeps your reading state, and duplicate chapters are merged safely.
* Fixed: logging in to the sync server on macOS.

## Security and privacy

* **Secure screen:** keep the app out of screenshots and the recent apps preview, always or only in incognito mode.
* **Lock after:** ask to authenticate after 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes away, or only when the app starts.

## Updates and first launch

* Onboarding starts by asking for your language.
* Clearer update dialog: installed and new version, date, size, sorted notes and what happens next. You will see it from the next update onwards.
* Pre-releases are now ordered correctly when checking for updates.
* New open source licenses screen in About.
* New Persian translation, and the missing strings translated in every language.

## Platforms

* **Android:** fixed a crash where all files access cannot be granted.
* **Android TV:** fixed the Player settings in the anime-only layout, and the repository added on the welcome screen is filed under anime.
* **iOS:** local files stay inside their folder.
* **macOS:** the app icon now fits the system's icon grid.
* **Windows:** sharper 256 px icon, used by the installer too, and more readable crash reports.
* **Linux:** choose which browser opens external links; JPEG is read whichever libjpeg version is installed; fixed webview window crashes.

## Stability and performance

* Faster database queries and lower memory use.
* The next chapter preloads on a new page rather than on every frame.
* A page that lost its data now offers a way back instead of crashing.
* The startup error screen says what to do when the database cannot open.
* Handled errors are now recorded, and developer mode shows them with their details.

## Contributors

Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release: @adobex, @aliafshany, @itsyaba, @Lukas-DS, @matsukiender-star, @MenaHere, @NBA2K1 and @Totara-thib.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/kodjodevf/mangayomi/compare/v0.9.9...v0.9.95

apps.name: MiniWatts
apps.subtitle: Battery, charging and thermal instrument
apps.localizedDescription: An iPhone battery and charging monitor built on Apple's private APIs: the charger's real watts, how much of that reaches the cell, where the rest goes as heat, and every temperature sensor in the phone. No network code — nothing it reads leaves your phone.

versions.localizedDescription:
Unsigned build — sign it with your own Apple ID before installing.
https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts#install

## 改进

- **温度可以显示为华氏度。** 设置 → 单位 里可选"自动 / °C / °F"。"自动"跟随系统地区，以及"设置 › 通用 › 语言与地区"里的"温度"选项，所以地区使用华氏度的用户升级后会直接看到 °F。App 各页、图表、热力图、悬浮读数、实时活动和小组件都按所选单位显示；原始数据仍显示传感器给出的 °C。(#25)
- **充电预估。** 充电时，功率页会显示充到 80% 和充到 100% 还要多久，以及大约几点。时间根据电量实际上升的速度推算，不依赖电池能量设置；要等电量变化两次才会出现，通常需要几分钟。80% 以后按典型充电曲线估算，只是近似值。(#27)
- **显示版本号。** 设置 → 关于 里显示当前版本，原始数据导出的第一行也带上了版本号。(#27)
- **iPad 布局。** iPad 横屏和 13 英寸竖屏时，各页分成两栏；窄屏时仍是一栏。历史记录里单次充电的详情页在 iPad 上不再横向铺满。(#22)
- **iPad 热力图。** 在 iPad 上，发热页画的是 iPad 的轮廓，各区域按 iPad Pro 11 英寸的内部布局放置：主板在中间，两侧是电芯，充电芯片在 USB-C 接口旁。设备页和设置里的图标也换成了 iPad。(#13, #22)

## 修复

- 发热：CPU 簇（`pACC`、`eACC`）和图像处理器（`ISP`）等传感器以前被归入"其他传感器"，现在算作 SoC，SoC 区域的温度也会把它们算进去。iPhone 11 上 `FrontCameraDie`、`BCMLBSkin` 这类名字连写的传感器以前会被分错区（比如前摄像头被当成机身），现在会先拆词再归类。(#13, #14)
- 适配器页里"单次采样"那段说明以前在中文界面下一直显示英文，现在已有中文。

## 注意

- iPad 相关的改动只在模拟器里验证过，我手上没有 iPad。如果在 iPad 上看到问题，请从 设置 → 原始数据 复制导出并反馈。
- iPad 上"来自充电器"的功率偏低（#13）这次还没有修：要确认其余的输入由哪个传感器测量，需要一份**充电时**导出的原始数据。有 iPad 的话，请在充电时从 设置 → 原始数据 复制导出，贴到 #13。
- 充电预估无法知道是否开启了充电上限或优化电池充电。如果开着，电池会在上限前停下，"充到 100%"的时间就不准。

---

## Improvements

- **Temperatures can be shown in Fahrenheit.** Settings → Units offers Automatic, °C or °F. Automatic follows your region and the Temperature option under Settings › General › Language & Region, so if your region uses Fahrenheit you will see °F straight after updating. Every page, the charts, the heat map, the floating meter, the Live Activity and the widget follow the setting; Raw data still shows the sensors' own °C. (#25)
- **Charge forecast.** While charging, the Power page shows how long until 80% and until 100%, and roughly when. It is worked out from how fast the battery level is actually rising, so it does not depend on the battery energy setting; it appears once the level has moved twice, usually within a few minutes. Past 80% it follows a typical charging curve and is approximate. (#27)
- **Version number.** Settings → About shows the installed version, and the first line of the Raw data dump includes it. (#27)
- **iPad layout.** On an iPad in landscape, and a 13-inch in portrait, every page uses two columns; narrower windows keep one. A session's detail page in History no longer stretches edge to edge on an iPad. (#22)
- **iPad heat map.** On an iPad the Thermal page draws an iPad, with the zones placed as in an iPad Pro 11-inch: logic board down the middle, a battery cell either side, the charge IC by the USB-C port. The Devices page and Settings use iPad icons too. (#13, #22)

## Fixes

- Thermal: the CPU-cluster (`pACC`, `eACC`) and image-processor (`ISP`) sensors used to land under "Other sensors"; they now count as the SoC, and the SoC zone's temperature includes them. On an iPhone 11, run-together sensor names such as `FrontCameraDie` and `BCMLBSkin` were filed in the wrong zone (the front camera as chassis); names are now split into words before they are matched. (#13, #14)
- Adapter: the one-sample note always showed in English in the Chinese interface; it is now translated.

## Notes

- The iPad changes were checked in the simulator only — I do not have an iPad. If something looks wrong on yours, copy the dump from Settings → Raw data and report it.
- The low "from charger" reading on an iPad (#13) is not fixed yet: finding which sensor carries the rest of the input needs a Raw data dump taken **while charging**. If you have an iPad, please copy one from Settings → Raw data while it charges and post it on #13.
- The charge forecast cannot tell whether a charge limit or Optimized Battery Charging is on. If one is, the battery stops short and the time to 100% will be wrong.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ResistanceTo/MiniWatts/compare/v1.6.0...v1.7.0

- The mini player no longer sits on top of the tab bar ([#118](https://github.com/verback2308/Opaline/issues/118)). Tapping a tab behind the collapsed player switches to that tab instead of reopening the video.
- Stereo no longer gets spatialized on AirPods ([#119](https://github.com/verback2308/Opaline/issues/119)). Ordinary two-channel sound was being turned into a fake surround field that moved when you turned your head. Video that really is multichannel still spatializes.

apps.subtitle: Apple Silicon macOS Ventura running inside an iPhone app
apps.localizedDescription: Boots a real arm64 macOS Ventura guest on iPhone through Apple's own chain (AVPBooter, iBoot and XNU) on QEMU's apple-vm machine, with the GPU drawn through Metal by reims-vgpu. versions.localizedDescription:
Orchard for iPhone 0.2: a faster emulator and a faster Metal path, plus a fix for guests that end up in Recovery.

Setup and settings: [README](https://github.com/MakrSas/orchard-ios#readme).

## Faster

On an iPhone 15 (A16), light scenes now reach 30–40 frames a second. Dragging a window runs at 10–15 frames a second (in 0.1 it dropped to around 7 once the Dock and menu bar were up).

- **CPU (QEMU TCG)**
  - The jump cache is bigger and better hashed, and keeps each process's blocks across context switches. Block-lookup misses fell from ~15% to ~3%.
  - Changing ASID flushes only the user half of the TLB.
  - The PMU is off, and fewer system-register writes end a translation block or flush the TLB.
- **Fast pointer authentication** (on by default, in Settings → Machine → Processor). The guest still sees PAC, but no signature is computed. That was 10–15% of the emulator's time. Turn it off if macOS stops booting.
- **Metal path (reims-vgpu)**
  - A guest render pass stays on the GPU as one Metal pass, instead of a GPU round trip, a full-frame readback and a re-upload for every draw.
  - Draw buffers come from a shared ring.
  - Shader keys hash faster.
  - Stores write back only the drawn area, with a NEON channel swap straight into guest pages.
- **Tip:** 960×540 at 30 Hz is the sweet spot. In the guest, Reduce transparency helps dragging windows.

## Fixed

- **Guest stuck in Recovery with no disk.** This was macOS installing an automatic update, which cannot complete on this machine. Turn automatic updates off first thing; the README has the settings and the Terminal commands.
- **Disk safety.** The disk is flushed when the app goes to the background and on Shut Down, and the log records guest flushes and I/O errors.

## Also since 0.1

- Sound (experimental, Settings → Machine → Sound).
- A shared folder: Files → Orchard → Shared, mounted in the guest at `http://10.0.2.2:8080`.
- Internet in the guest works.

## You need

- iOS 16 or later, tested on an iPhone 15 with iOS 27, and a phone with 6 GB of memory or more.
- A signing tool that adds the increased memory limit capability, and JIT (such as StikDebug).
- A macOS 13 VM made in UTM on a Mac.

Blizzard through Playport's new **Battle.net** store, sign in and step into Azeroth. **Red
Dead Redemption 2** rides out of Arthur's cabin, **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered**
plays in Kaer Morhen, and **no controller is needed any more**: on-screen touch controls
with three layouts, a full layout editor, a touch keyboard, controller mapping and gyro
aim. Add a redesigned Library, a performance overlay and Vulkan for every game.

> **❤️ Playport is free, and it stays free. If it put a PC game in your pocket, please
> consider [supporting it on Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/playportdev).** Getting World of
> Warcraft, Red Dead Redemption 2 and The Witcher 3 running on a phone took a lot of work,
> and every donation buys time for the next release: more games and more fixes.
>
> [![Support Playport on Ko-fi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Support_Playport-on_Ko--fi-FF5E5B?style=for-the-badge&logo=kofi&logoColor=white)](https://ko-fi.com/playportdev)
>
> A donation is a gift: it buys no licence, no extra rights and no different build, and
> everyone may keep sharing Playport under its licence.

**Updated IPA (2 November 2026).** The 0.5.0 IPA was replaced with a build that adds three
fixes:

- 32-bit games that unpack their own code at start-up (The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, The
  Witcher 2) no longer crash before their first frame.
- Playport's Steam client now gives a game Steam's ownership ticket, so The Witcher 2's DRM
  check passes.
- A tap on a launcher's window goes to what you see under your finger: The Witcher 2
  launcher's **Launch game** works.

If you installed 0.5.0 before this, download it again. `SHA256SUMS` lists the new files.

![World of Warcraft in the world with the on-screen Keyboard & mouse controls and the performance overlay](https://playport.dev/screenshots/wow-touch.webp)

## Highlights

### ⚔️ World of Warcraft, from Battle.net
**Battle.net is now a store in Playport**, next to Steam, GOG and Epic Games, and World of
Warcraft shows in everyone's Library. No Battle.net app and no sign-in in Playport: pick
the game, press Install, and Playport downloads it from Blizzard's own servers.

- **Retail, Classic, Classic Era and Classic Anniversary**, each with a region picker (US,
  Europe, Korea or Taiwan; your phone's region by default) and a language. Playport checks
  the free space before it starts and installs through Downloads, with pause, resume and
  cancel.
- **Always up to date:** every Play checks for a new build first and updates through
  Downloads, then plays. *Check for update* sits on the game's page too.
- **The game signs itself in**, as on a PC. The in-game menu's new **Type text** opens a
  field over the game for your email, password and authenticator code, with paste and
  AutoFill.
- **It plays.** In our testing World of Warcraft reaches its login screen within about
  45 seconds of Play and runs in the world at **55–60 FPS**.
- **Your game, untouched:** Playport runs Blizzard's own Windows client through its
  translator and changes none of the game's files and none of its code in memory. Before
  the first Play it tells you plainly that Blizzard does not support Playport.

![The Library's Battle.net store with World of Warcraft](https://playport.dev/screenshots/library-battlenet.webp)

### 🤠 Red Dead Redemption 2 rides
Press Play and Rockstar's own launcher starts, signs in, hands the game its ticket and gets
out of the way. Social Club runs on Rockstar's own components, so the game stays signed in
and saves as it should. One press on Story and you are in Arthur's cabin, on the frontier,
on a phone.

![Arthur Morgan in a winter coat on a snowy cabin porch, snow-covered pines beyond](https://playport.dev/screenshots/rdr2.webp)

### 🐺 The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered plays
The remastered 4.x build of The Witcher 3 used to stop the moment it started: it needs
AVX instructions the phone could not offer and asks for far more memory space than an
iPhone app gets. Playport now handles both, and Geralt is back in Kaer Morhen, on the
game's Direct3D 12 renderer. The classic 1.32 build still plays as before.

![Geralt walking through a hall of Kaer Morhen past a lit fireplace](https://playport.dev/screenshots/witcher3-remastered.webp)

### 🎮 On-screen controls: play with nothing but the phone
No controller? Playport draws its **on-screen controls** over the game. Connect a controller
and they step aside; disconnect it and they come back (*Settings › Controls*: Automatic,
Always or Never).

- **Three layouts, plus Off:** **Gamepad** (sticks, d-pad, A/B/X/Y, bumpers, triggers, View
  and Menu), **Keyboard & mouse** (a W A S D stick, drag anywhere free to look, key caps
  around your thumb) and **Point & click** (tap to click or use it as a trackpad, with a
  magnifier for small targets, plus right click, hover, scroll, keys and Esc).
- **A three-finger tap** anywhere opens Playport's in-game menu, with any layout. The first
  time the controls appear on their own, a toast says so.
- **The layout editor:** add, move, resize, duplicate and remove controls on a grid with
  snapping guides, undo, reset and switch presets, by touch or with a controller, over the
  paused game or from *Game options › Controls*. Each game keeps its own layout and its own
  opacity.
- **A suggested starting layout:** a game that never asks for a controller in its first
  20 seconds is offered Keyboard & mouse, once.
- **A touch keyboard** over the game, with F keys, arrows and sticky Shift, Ctrl and Alt,
  for consoles, names and the keys a layout lacks.
- **Any controller as a keyboard and mouse:** *Game options › Controls › Controller* maps
  every button, stick, trigger and gyro to a controller input, a key with modifiers, a
  mouse button, mouse movement or the wheel, or a Playport action. Pick **As a controller**,
  **As keyboard & mouse** or **Custom**.
- **Gyro aim:** aim by moving the phone, or a DualSense, DualShock 4 or Switch Pro
  controller, as the mouse or the right stick, per game, with sensitivity, smoothing and a
  test area to try it before you play.

![The layout editor over World of Warcraft, editing the Keyboard & mouse layout](https://playport.dev/screenshots/touch-editor.webp)

![World of Warcraft on a ship's deck with a blue dragon mount, with the on-screen Gamepad layout](https://playport.dev/screenshots/wow-gamepad.webp)

### 📚 A redesigned Library
The stores are now **a column of icons down the Library's left**: All, Steam, GOG, Epic
Games and Battle.net, every one always there (a store you are signed out of is dimmed).
The chosen store's name and game count sit above the grid, and **Installed only** narrows
any of them with one tap. With a controller, press left from the first column to reach the
stores, or step through them from anywhere with LT and RT.

![The Library with All games and the store column](https://playport.dev/screenshots/library-0.5.webp)

### 📊 A performance overlay
A small pill at the top of the game shows the **frame rate, the frame time and your phone's
thermal state**. Turn it on from the in-game menu or *Settings › Graphics*, and it stays on
for every game. It replaces Apple's Metal HUD, which cost CPU time on every frame.

## Also new
- **Vulkan is every game's graphics backend.** Direct3D 9, 10, 11 and 12 now run on Vulkan
  over Metal by default. DXMT stays one choice away in *Settings › Graphics › Direct3D* or
  on the game's page.
- **Quicker launches:** shaders are compiled faster for Metal on iOS 27, and what the
  graphics backends and the code translator have done is kept on disk, so a second launch
  skips the first one's work. *Settings › Storage › Shader cache* shows the space and
  clears it.
- **OpenGL games run**, through Mesa's Zink on Vulkan, in 64-bit and 32-bit games alike.
- **More room for big games:** each Play's memory is planned from your phone's memory and
  the game's needs, freed memory is reused, and *Settings › Graphics › Donor memory*
  (Auto by default) lets a game use more than the app alone could hold.
- **Steam for 32-bit games too:** Playport's own Steam client now serves 32-bit games the
  same sign-in, ownership check and online tickets as 64-bit ones. **Repair** fetches
  missing Steamworks Shared files.
- **Games get what they need, from Play:** an *Installing dependencies* step runs a game's
  own prerequisite installer once, fetches Steam's or GOG's redistributables, and carries
  Wine Mono for .NET games.
- **Publisher launchers:** Rockstar's launcher runs for the games that need it, and a
  game's own launcher and dialog windows show instead of an empty screen.
- **Type text** in the in-game menu sends typing, paste and AutoFill to the game's focused
  field, with a password mode.
- **Graphics choices are cleaner:** *Aspect ratio* and *Resolution* are separate, and a
  game can carry its own compatibility defaults (Super Meat Boy's 16:9, Assassin's Creed's
  Keyboard & mouse layout).
- **Screenshot** works over Vulkan games, and games that change display mode keep showing.
- **Settings scrolls** on a landscape phone; *Storage* lists Steamworks Shared, the shader
  cache and the translator's cache with their sizes.
- **Newer components:** Wine 11.20 with Valve's latest Proton Wine changes, and current
  FEX (the translator that runs x86 code on the phone), DXMT, DXVK, vkd3d-proton and Mesa.

## Games
The [compatibility list](https://playport.dev/compatibility/) carries every game we and
players have tried. Running since 0.4.0:

- **Runs:** Among Us, Assassin's Creed: Director's Cut Edition, BioShock (GOG), Monster
  Train (GOG), Duck Paradox (GOG), Spelunky (GOG), Tomb Raider: Anniversary (GOG), Super
  Meat Boy (Epic), Soccer Online: Ball 3D, #DRIVE Rally, Castle Crashers (demo), Cat Mail
  Co. (demo) and Football Manager 2022's Resource Archiver.
- **Runs, with issues listed on their pages:** Counter-Strike and Half-Life (OpenGL),
  Neverwinter Nights: Enhanced Edition (GOG), Tomb Raider (2013), DiRT 3 Complete Edition,
  House of Golf 2 (Epic), and the three in the highlights: World of Warcraft, Red Dead
  Redemption 2 and The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered.

## Good to know
- **World of Warcraft needs your Battle.net account** with an active subscription; the
  game's own login checks it. Blizzard does not support Playport, and an action on your
  account is possible: Playport asks you to accept that once before the first Play.
- **World of Warcraft is big:** retail needs about 132 GB of free space, Classic about
  80 GB and Classic Era about 5 GB. Our testing covered retail. Busy cities and raids may
  run slower than the open world.
- **Red Dead Redemption 2 and The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Remastered push the phone to its
  limits.** Both run close to the app's memory limit and need the increased memory limit
  from your sideloader. Both heat the phone, and their frame rate drops as it warms;
  expect long loads and hitches. Red Dead Redemption 2 installs about 120 GB, and we test
  Story mode only, never Red Dead Online. In bright light some highlights look wrong (a
  white beard brim, a red ear).
- **Vulkan is the default now.** If a game looks or behaves worse than on 0.4.0, switch it
  to **DXMT** on its page (*Game options › Graphics › Direct3D*) and tell us which game.
- **On-screen controls:** without a controller, the three-finger tap is the only way into
  the in-game menu. In some games' menus a Point & click tap moves the highlight without
  opening the item (Portal 2's). A game may show controller prompts while the layout is
  Off. Gyro aim drives the game's own stick or mouse, so a game's own aim settings still
  apply.
- **Big games keep needing memory,** and a game that wants more than the phone can hold
  still ends.
- **Tested on one phone** (iOS 27.2). If a game misbehaves, *Report a problem* on its page
  shares one zip with its logs.
- Your games, saves and logins are untouched by this update; install over 0.4.0.

## Install

Download `Playport-0.5.0.ipa` and sideload it with your own Apple ID, keeping the
increased memory limit and the JIT helper extension. If you have an earlier version,
install over it: your games, saves and logins stay. Bring your own games from Steam, GOG,
Epic Games or Files, or install World of Warcraft from Battle.net.

The complete Corresponding Source of this exact build, the notices and the rebuild
instructions are attached as `Playport-0.5.0-source.tar`, `NOTICES.tar` and
`INSTALL-REBUILD.tar`. `SHA256SUMS` covers every file.

# RewindBox 0.0.11 — Build 721

Everything since RewindBox 0.0.10 (Build 559), brought together in one update.

## 🎮 PlayStation 3 — RPCS3

- **Assassin’s Creed:** audio mixing corrections prevent audio periods from being discarded during waits.
- Reduced redundant rendering interruptions and repeated graphics work, including changes to **Vulkan/MoltenVK**.
- Improved texture caching to reuse more previously calculated results.
- **Black Ops II:** corrections to SPU synchronization, memory reservations and waits involved in stalls.
- **Black Ops II:** earlier submission of pending occlusion results, with a separate bounded budget, targets waits on the game’s main CPU threads.
- Corrected short active-wait timing on iPhones with a 1 GHz system counter and adjusted the BO2 writer-lock wait path.
- **Assassin’s Creed:** corrected an atomic SPU write that could overwrite a newer main-CPU value during game exit.
- Improved SPU program preparation and cache reuse to reduce recompilation during gameplay.
- **God of War III:** removed the unintended 30 FPS limit and reduced unnecessary texture validation.
- **God of War III v1.00:** the optional MLAA bypass now applies on a fresh boot as well.
- **Assassin’s Creed IV and Dynasty Warriors 6:** corrected game profiles to use the LLVM PPU recompiler.
- Corrected texture coherence, partial graphics commands and CPU/GPU synchronization paths.
- More reliable retention of mounted ISO images.
- Corrected JIT memory reservation when the usual address range is unavailable, including on certain iOS beta versions.
- Repositioned the **Menu** and **Performance** buttons to better respect touch controls and safe areas.
- Expanded per-game settings and diagnostic tools to identify the causes of stalls more precisely.

## 🎨 Skins and touch controls

- Added **GameCube Pocket, Wii Pocket and PS2 Pocket** skins.
- Added **Pocket — Original** variants for GameCube, Wii and PS2 while keeping the existing designs.
- Added **Switch Pocket**, available through **Skins in the Switch playlist menu**.
- Portrait and landscape layouts, with orientation locking where supported by the selected skin and engine.
- Corrected offsets between the drawn buttons and their touch areas.
- Corrected **rectangular press highlights**, pressed states and analog-stick geometry.
- GameCube/Wii analog sticks now move as a complete circle, including the C-stick.
- Bundled skin updates now refresh older installed copies while preserving your selections.
- Restored access to **Skins from the PS2 playlist**.
- Corrected the return from the MeloNX in-game menu so skin buttons and sticks regain input immediately.
- Improved game-screen framing inside Pocket skins, including rounded corners.
- Refined pressed-button visuals so controls sink into their housings rather than simply turning gray.
- Dolphin and PS2 floating session buttons no longer cover skin controls when the skin provides its own Menu button.

## 🏆 RetroAchievements

- Centralized sign-in and **Hardcore** settings.
- Corrected repeated sign-outs, credential persistence and migration of older accounts.
- Improved session ownership of notifications and progress, including external-display presentation.
- Achievement text follows the app language when the required Apple translation features are available.
- Improved game recognition, including **CHD and CSO**, with consistent identification in the library and during play.
- Clearer messages distinguish an unrecognized game from an unreadable file.

## 🧩 Cheats & Enhancements

- A unified **Cheats & Enhancements** page for each game.
- Access to compatible frame-rate, aspect-ratio, graphics and other available game patches.
- Improved activation, deactivation and restoration of original settings.
- **Corrected unintended Switch cheat activation** when the enable list was missing.
- Cheat state remains usable after the app container moves.
- RewindBox-generated cheat files now contain only the selected programs.

## 📚 Library, artwork and manuals

- Reworked 3D cases with more faithful proportions, relief, spines and backs.
- Editable back covers and nondestructive image correction.
- Artwork matching using the ROM’s actual game identifier.
- More reliable batch scraping with better preservation of existing media.
- Improved **French cover and manual** lookup with additional sources.
- Improved scan viewing and zoom.
- Lighter Switch discovery avoids reading entire game files on the main thread.

## ✨ Interface and navigation

- New **RewindBox Glacier** style with a reversible preset.
- Bundled offline system artwork.
- Corrections to margins, obscured titles, icon sizes and carousels.
- Corrections to system bubbles and the “⋯” menu.
- An **icons-only main navigation bar**, while retaining accessible names for VoiceOver.

## 🧪 Experimental renderer

- Added an **optional native Metal 4 renderer for RPCS3**. Vulkan/MoltenVK remains available and the selected renderer is preserved.

## Testing and known limits

The downloaded Build 721 IPA passed the recorded offline package, source/component identity and delivery checks. RPCS3 Core 919. Fresh Flutter, native and delivery-contract checks were executed for this delivery. The downloaded file matches the original private delivery byte for byte.

Automated tests and desktop benchmarks do not establish iPhone FPS, audio or gameplay improvements. The complete package has not been gameplay-validated on a physical iPhone. First-use shader compilation and game-specific issues may remain. Cheats and achievement support depend on the game, version and engine.

Long Hogwarts Legacy pauses and residual BO2 performance problems remain under investigation. This build retains automatic BO2/God of War III comparison windows; their removal belongs to a later build and is not included here.

Some faithful Pocket layouts have small touch targets or Dynamic Island overlap. Switch Pocket’s HOME and Capture controls are unavailable in this engine; MeloNX does not lock session orientation through the skin. The MeloNX Metal binary-archive prototype, Switch 2 experiment and RPCS3 comparison-only Cores are not included.

## Download and installation

**IPA:** [RewindBox-0.0.11.ipa](https://github.com/TarbleFR/RewindBox/releases/download/0.0.11/RewindBox-0.0.11.ipa)

**SideStore / AltStore Classic source:** [source.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TarbleFR/RewindBox/Claude/source.json)

- Requires **iOS 18.0 or later**.
- Re-sign with SideStore, AltStore Classic or your usual compatible sideloading tool. This is not a notarized AltStore PAL package or a directly installable Apple distribution build.
- Public release: **0.0.11**. IPA metadata remains **0.0.8, Build 721**; the source preserves those exact values and uses `marketingVersion` to display 0.0.11.
- Size: **267,033,667 bytes**.
- SHA-256: `bc640a83a01de8a623c16fb0b5977edf16ac6010b61c9c2489ae334d3db3c0d7`.

No firmware, keys, BIOS or game files are bundled.
